title: 1-to-4 Demultiplexer: One Data Bit, Four Possible Outputs
topic: 1-to-4 demultiplexer — one data input D, two select bits S1 and S0, and four outputs Y0 through Y3; the select bits address which output gets the input value, the others are forced to zero; the dual of a multiplexer

beats.narration: One data line in, four possible outputs out — how do two select bits decide where the bit goes?

elements.content: One bit in, four outputs out — only one wakes up.

beats.narration: A demultiplexer has one data input D, two select bits S one and S zero, and four output lines Y zero through Y three. Inside, four AND gates fed by a small decoder pick exactly one output to wake up.

elements.content: Demux block diagram: D input on left, S1 and S0 select inputs below, four output lines Y0..Y3 on the right; inner AND gates with decoder lines feeding each gate's select pin

beats.narration: The rule is short. The output addressed by the two select bits takes the value of D; every other output is held at zero. Read down the truth table and a single column of ones tracks the select address.

elements.content: 4-row truth table with S1 S0 | Y0 Y1 Y2 Y3, the diagonal of D values lighting the addressed column

beats.narration: Cycle the two select bits through zero zero, zero one, one zero, one one. The active output line slides from Y zero to Y three in lockstep — and whatever D is doing rides on top.

elements.content: Demux schematic with live S1/S0 readout cycling 00→01→10→11; active output line glowing amber and showing D's value; inactive lines greyed at 0

beats.narration: A demultiplexer broadcasts one wire onto many, addressed by select bits. Combined with a multiplexer it is how a single bus reaches many destinations.
